transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-07 08:00 PT | Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Head of ML, Northwind), Lena Ortiz (Platform Lead), Diego Morales (CTO)
Recording note: internal audio; some overlap and crosstalk; auto-summary present below

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Northwind wants to validate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for a pilot that must hit a tight budget and 95th pctl latency under 300ms for chat-like flows.
- Discussed per-token pricing, batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization, and routing fallbacks.
- Redwood to send pilot pricing + run baseline cost scenarios; Northwind to share request mix and latency objectives.

Topics:
- Pilot sizing & budget lanes
- Per-token unit economics and batching impact
- KV cache/prefix cache benefits for multi-turn chat
- Hosted vs Dedicated (dedicated GPU pools) vs Private/VPC constraints
- Compliance needs & artifacts (SOC2, network diagram)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex Chen from Redwood. I have Priya with me, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Samir Patel: Doing well, thanks. Excited to dive in, we, uh, we've been trying to — I mean we looked at some of your docs.
[00:10] Lena Ortiz: Hi, Alex, Priya. Quick context: we're scoping a two-month pilot to validate unit economics for a customer-facing chat assistant. Budget is tight; expectation is we can't exceed $X per month for inference. Will share specifics in a sec.
[00:23] Alex Chen: Great. Can you say what the target budget number is, and any latency SLAs or p95 targets?
[00:27] Lena Ortiz: Budget we can commit for pilot is $18k/month for inference only. Latency goal is p95 under ~300ms for short conversations, but we can tolerate p99 spikes during peak.
[00:37] Diego Morales: Also we have SAML SSO, SOC2 is required but not blocking pilot. We're evaluating hosted first, but we might need private if data residency becomes an issue.
[00:45] Priya Desai: Cool. To make this concrete, can you share your expected request mix (avg tokens in and out), concurrency, and any multi-turn retention? Even ballpark helps.
[00:52] Samir Patel: Sure — rough numbers: 1M requests/day at peak planning horizon, but pilot will be ~100k requests/day. Avg input tokens 30, output tokens 90 -> roughly 120 total tokens per request. Multi-turn window ~3 turns, and we want the ability to cache KV for repeated prefixes for faster outputs.
[01:12] Alex Chen: Nice, good baseline. Quick high-level: per-token pricing + batching + KV caching will be the main levers. Hosted is fastest to start; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and can drop unit cost in many workloads by allowing aggressive batching and GPU utilization; Private/VPC is for data residency and stricter network controls and adds ops overhead.
[01:30] Samir Patel: On unit economics, we're most interested in a per-1k-token price equivalent. Can you walk us through a sample calculation for both Hosted and Dedicated?
[01:36] Priya Desai: Yeah, quick sketch. For Hosted, we have published per-token rates for model families — I'll send the exact SKU — but conceptually: Hosted = base per-token + small infra fee, with less ability for you to control batching. For Dedicated, you pre-reserve a GPU pool; depending on batch depth and KV cache hit-rate, your per-token can drop 20–50%.
[01:52] Lena Ortiz: That 20–50% is a big range. What assumptions drive that?
[01:57] Priya Desai: Mainly batch size, request concurrency, and cache hit-rate. Example: if you average 8-12 tokens per request and can batch 32 requests per GPU step at 1ms per token (hardware-dependent), your amortized cost per token halves vs small batch 1–4. KV cache is huge for multi-turn: if you can reuse cached KV for prefix compute 40% of tokens are served from cache, that portion is near-zero incremental compute. So with 40% cache hit and decent batching, you see the high end of savings.
[02:28] Samir Patel: For our pilot numbers — 120 tokens per request, 100k req/day — what's a back-of-the-envelope monthly token volume and cost?
[02:34] Alex Chen: 100k * 120 = 12M tokens/day -> wait that's per day. For a 30-day month that's 360M tokens. Does that align with your pilot?
[02:44] Samir Patel: Sorry I misspoke — pilot will be 100k/day peak for a few days, average 30k/day across the month. So let's assume 30k * 120 = 3.6M tokens/day -> ~108M tokens/month.
[02:57] Priya Desai: Using rough hosted rates for the model family you're targeting — say $0.00035 per token (example placeholder) — that'd be ~ $37.8k/month on hosted. With Dedicated and 30–40% KV cache + batching, that could compress to around $18k–24k/month. We'll run exact math in the spreadsheet with real SKUs.
[03:18] Lena Ortiz: That helps. We're curious about burst patterns — we need certain troughs/peaks for marketing events. How does capacity/fallback work with Dedicated?
[03:25] Alex Chen: Dedicated has baseline reserved capacity with optional burst capacity into hosted pool. We can configure automatic fallback rules so if dedicated is saturated, requests route to hosted model variants potentially at a different unit cost and latency. You can also set routing by latency or cost policy.
[03:38] Diego Morales: For private/VPC, is the per-token cost higher because of smaller cluster sizes and more ops?
[03:44] Priya Desai: Typically, Private has additional platform fees and you bear infra operating costs; unit compute cost may be similar at scale but the initial fixed costs are higher. For a pilot at 100k/day average, Private often doesn't make sense unless you need residency/compliance.
[03:57] Samir Patel: OK. Could you explain KV cache more — I'm not sure I fully get the mechanics and the limits?
[04:02] Priya Desai: Sure — KV cache stores key/value tensors for earlier token compute for a particular conversation prefix. In chat, when you re-use earlier system prompts or repeating user prompts, we can avoid recomputing the entire prefix. Two practical points: cache hit-rate depends on how similar requests are; it helps a lot for templated flows. Second, cache is per-model-version and per-customer or per-route depending on your privacy config. In Dedicated, you can tune cache size and eviction policies.
[04:28] Lena Ortiz: So if we have a chat where 60% of requests reuse prefixes, does that mean 60% of tokens are free?
[04:33] Priya Desai: Not entirely free — there's small retrieval overhead and some memory bandwidth cost — but compute-heavy attention/transformer passes are skipped for cached tokens. It's often modeled as near-zero incremental compute for the cached portion. We'll model this conservatively when we run the scenarios.
[04:47] Alex Chen: Also, prefix cache vs full KV cache — sometimes initial tokens (system + initial user context) are common and those benefit the most.
[04:54] Samir Patel: Good. Another angle — quantization. We currently train with fp16 but were curious if you recommend 8-bit quantized variants for cost savings and how much that changes latency.
[05:02] Priya Desai: We support quantized runtimes; 8-bit int can reduce GPU memory and allow larger batch sizes, improving throughput. Latency per token might be slightly higher per kernel depending on hardware, but overall unit cost often drops. For latency-sensitive p95 under 300ms, we'd run a benchmark — on some models 8-bit has negligible latency impact; on others there's a small tail. We'll test both.
[05:21] Diego Morales: For the pilot we need a clear success criteria. I propose: 1) demonstration of expected unit cost within 10% of forecast, 2) p95 <= 300ms on Dedicated or Hosted with fallback, 3) security artifacts provided. Agree?
[05:31] Alex Chen: Sounds good. We'll reflect that in the SOW.
[05:34] Lena Ortiz: What about throttling and token quotas — if we hit budget cap, can we limit throughput with routing to smaller models or degrade gracefully?
[05:41] Priya Desai: Yes — Redwood supports per-route throttling, model fallback, and degrade policies. For instance, when cost threshold hits, you can route to smaller model family or change max tokens/tokenizer settings. We can set automatic rules to keep within a monthly cap.
[05:53] Samir Patel: Can you give an example of an automated policy?
[05:55] Priya Desai: Example: When monthly spend on Route A exceeds 75% of pilot budget, route new requests to a quantized 7B variant with lower per-token cost, preserve critical routes to big model only for priority traffic. We'll show a sample rule in the console.
[06:08] Alex Chen: Quick note: we've seen customers combine prefix caching and conservative batching to get 40–60% effective token savings for conversational tasks. That's where Dedicated really shines because you control GPU utilization.
[06:18] Samir Patel: About the pricing spreadsheet — can you post an example so our finance folks can flip the knobs?
[06:22] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll share a pilot pricing spreadsheet with line items for hosted delta, dedicated baseline, pilot credits, and expected per-token bands. Link: https://redwood.ai/pilot-pricing/nwv (internal preview link).
[06:34] Lena Ortiz: We may also run a compliance review — we need SOC2, network diagram, and KMS integration notes. Can you include that in your follow-up?
[06:40] Priya Desai: Absolutely. We'll attach SOC2 summary and a network diagram for both Hosted (what we manage) and Private/VPC (customer-managed).
[06:48] Diego Morales: One more thing: can Dedicated do per-tenant isolation if we were to serve multiple lines of business?
[06:52] Priya Desai: Yes, Dedicated supports tenant pools and strict isolation; you can pin models and routing to a pool. There's config for quotas and RBAC.
[06:59] Samir Patel: Great. A few clarifying edge cases: 1) If cache gets evicted during high churn, does that spike costs? 2) For multi-turn context that grows beyond 2k tokens, do you recompute prefix?
[07:11] Priya Desai: 1) Eviction can cause bursts of recompute; we can set eviction policies for important prefixes. 2) If context exceeds model window, you'd summarize or trim — we can help with strategies like on-the-fly summarization to reduce token footprint and cost.
[07:25] Alex Chen: Okay, for next steps we'll: send the pilot pricing + SOW, run token-cost scenarios with conservative and optimistic caching assumptions, and schedule a lab for a Dedicated baseline. Samir, Lena — you'll share request traces and SLOs.
[07:38] Samir Patel: Yes, I'll prepare two weeks of anonymized traces and a short doc with our p95/p99 targets.
[07:43] Lena Ortiz: We'll also loop in security for the SOC2 doc review.
[07:46] Diego Morales: Sounds good. Any blockers for starting?
[07:49] Priya Desai: None from our side. We'll prepare the configs and propose dates for the lab.
[07:54] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the links and the sheet.
[07:58] Samir Patel: Thanks, appreciate it.
